title:
Planted by
the Rivers
paragraphs: Before the psalm ever mentions a tree, it spends its first breath on refusal. Blessed is the one who will not walk, will not stand, will not sit — three postures of the body revealing the posture of the heart, long before fruit ever enters the conversation. We want the harvest without the discipline that precedes it, forgetting that the tree didn't earn its fruit by growing near water; it earned it by refusing to grow anywhere else. Every no you've had to say to counsel that sounded wise but wasn't is doing more for your future than you can currently see.

That's why verse three can promise fruit "in his season" and leave it there — not every season, not on demand, but exactly when it's ready. A tree planted by rivers of water doesn't produce because the drought never comes; it produces because its roots go deeper than the drought can reach. Stop measuring whether you're blessed by how fast you're fruiting, and start measuring it by what you've refused to be planted beside. The rivers were always feeding roots you can't see long before they fed any leaf everyone else could.
